claim.summary: Over F2, for every m>n>=0, the Boolean rank equations AB=I_m admit an explicit Hilbert-like IPS certificate built with one shared child of shape (m-1,n-1), first-nonzero pivot selectors and all Boolean mux/field corrections. Size obeys S(m,n)<=S(m-1,n-1)+poly(m,n), and depth O(n); joint placeholder degree is at most 3^n(n+1)!. Normalization gives a full residual certificate of polynomial size and depth O(n), with no constant-depth guarantee or original-PC-degree preservation. A seven-fixture native Singular checker verifies all local matrix/field maps and negative controls.

Direct Hilbert-like normalization additionally lies in the (m-1)-st power of the matrix-B ideal, so fixed-order B jets at B=0 vanish for large m; this is not a statement about arbitrary residual representatives. No new general rank-principle IPS upper-bound novelty claimed.

A general IPS certificate of size S/depth d yields a circuit Q(x,Z), linear in Z, with Q(x,0)=0 and Q(x,B)=A, at polynomial size in S+s+n+m and depth O(d+Delta+1). Conversely Q yields a full certificate with input coefficients F_i^(p-2) product_(l<i)(1-F_l^(p-1)). claim.summary: Determinant polynomials over F2 have no polynomial-size fixed-depth arithmetic circuits with binary constants, by an explicit affine reduction of MOD3 to two determinants of order 2n+3 and addition of one. For A=[[0,1],[1,1]], M_i=I+x_i(A-I), the trace product detects weight not divisible by3; each diagonal entry is det([[T,b_u],[-c_u^T,0]]) for upper block-bidiagonal T with I_2 diagonal and -M_i superdiagonal. Thus universal cheap binary canonical extraction on padded permutation CNFs and cheap binary extraction of its degree-r component cannot both hold.
claim.assessment: Working explicit standard circuit-reduction consequence of Smolensky Theorem2, medium reviewed. No independent novelty. The conjunction obstruction does not identify which operation fails on the particular family; padded formulas themselves have cheap certificates. Extension constants excluded.

The obstruction covers black-box binary scalar extraction, not white-box transformations or extension-field circuits.
